tier1.text: The cell membrane, also called the plasma membrane, separates the inside of a cell from the outside. The membrane forms a protective barrier around the cell and controls what passes in or out. Two layers of phospholipids, molecules with a head and two tails, make up the membrane. Membrane proteins form channels that let materials through and act as markers that identify the cell.

figures.title: Cell Membrane
figures.caption: The cell membrane of the cell is a phospholipid bilayer containing many different molecular components, including proteins and cholesterol, some with carbohydrate groups attached.
figures.alt: This image shows a lipid bilayer with different types of proteins, lipids and cholesterol embedded in it.
